effects: UTF-8 validation returns false at the first invalid code point; sanitization replaces each invalid UTF-8 sequence unit with underscore. On POSIX, direct convert returns the input unchanged when it is empty, returns an empty string if iconv_open cannot create the requested conversion, grows its output buffer on E2BIG, and on EILSEQ skips one offending input byte while writing underscore at the current output slot; other iconv errors replace remaining input bytes with underscores. POSIX toUtf8/fromUtf8 return nonempty input unchanged when their charset argument is empty (assuming system encoding is UTF-8); with a nonempty charset they call convert. Windows toUtf8/fromUtf8 use platform code-page conversion and return empty output when the platform conversion call fails. Direct convert passes its charset strings to the platform conversion API, so the empty-charset passthrough applies specifically to toUtf8/fromUtf8, not direct convert.
errors: Conversion failures are represented by an empty string, not an exception; malformed UTF-8 makes validateUtf8 return false. The POSIX EILSEQ path skips one offending input byte and writes an underscore at the current output slot before continuing.
